title: Daily Life - Living With Your Parents

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Kathryn and today we're talking about a special kind of man.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们谈论的是一个特殊的人。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Today we are, well, everyone starts living with your parents but as adults, some people still want to continue living with their parents.
segments.zh: 今天我们是，嗯，每个人都开始和你的父母住在一起，但作为成年人，有些人仍然想继续和父母一起生活。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So the topic of today's lesson is living with your parents when you're an adult.
segments.zh: 所以今天课程的主题是当你成年时和你的父母住在一起。

segments.en: Let's take a listen to the dialogue.
segments.zh: 让我们听听对话。

segments.en: Why did your girlfriend break up with you?
segments.zh: 为什么你的女朋友和你分手了？

segments.en: I don't know.
segments.zh: 我不知道。

segments.en: She said she was tired of me not manning up and being more independent, which I think is all a bunch of crap.
segments.zh: 她说受够了我不肯成熟独立，可我觉得那全是胡说八道。

segments.en: Well, you still live with your parents so she does have a point.
segments.zh: 可你现在还跟父母住，她说得也有道理。

segments.en: What do you mean?
segments.zh: 你是什么意思？

segments.en: A lot of people live with their parents, especially when rent is so expensive and the slump in the economy.
segments.zh: 现在房租那么贵，经济又不景气，很多人都和父母住。

segments.en: Yeah, but you're almost 40.
segments.zh: 可你都快四十了！

segments.en: Plus, you make good money so there's really no excuse.
segments.zh: 而且你收入不错，根本没借口。

segments.en: That's just simply because you're a mama's boy.
segments.zh: 说白了，你就是个妈宝男。

segments.en: Whatever, dude.
segments.zh: 随你怎么说吧，哥们儿。

segments.en: I have everything I need.
segments.zh: 我什么都不缺。

segments.en: Why would I move out?
segments.zh: 干吗要搬出去？

segments.en: Have a great roof over my head, my mom does my laundry and cooks for me.
segments.zh: 住得舒舒服服，妈妈还给我洗衣做饭。

segments.en: What else could a guy ask for?
segments.zh: 一个男人还能求什么？

segments.en: Let's agree to disagree.
segments.zh: 看来我们只能各持己见了。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now let's take a look at some language on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们来看看语言要点的一些表达。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: The first verb we have here is to break up.
segments.zh: 我们这里的第一个动词是分手。

segments.en: So we heard the guy say, why did your girlfriend break up with you?
segments.zh: 所以我们听到那个人说，你的女朋友为什么要和你分手？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So this is a phrasal verb and to break up in a relationship or in a romantic sense means to end a relationship.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个短语动词，在关系中或在浪漫意义上分手意味着结束一段关系。

segments.en: So if you break up with your girlfriend, it means you end the relationship.
segments.zh: 所以如果你和你的女朋友分手，这意味着你结束了这段关系。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you think about breaking something, it goes into pieces.
segments.zh: 所以你考虑打破一些东西，它会碎成碎片。

segments.en: Well, in a relationship, it means you both leave each other, you go your separate ways.
segments.zh: 好吧，在一段关系中，这意味着你们俩都离开了彼此，你们分道扬镳。

segments.en: And so you can say, he broke up with me or we broke up.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，他和我分手了，或者我们分手了。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And the reason his girlfriend broke up with him is because she said he was not independent.
segments.zh: 而他的女朋友和他分手的原因是因为她说他不独立。

segments.en: So she wanted him to be more independent.
segments.zh: 所以她希望他更加独立。

segments.en: So independent means that you do things on your own.
segments.zh: 所以独立意味着你自己做事。

segments.en: When you're, you know, you do things alone.
segments.zh: 当你是，你知道，你一个人做事。

segments.en: You don't expect other people to help you.
segments.zh: 你不希望其他人帮助你。

segments.en: You don't depend on other people.
segments.zh: 你不依赖别人。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So you can say, he's very independent.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，他非常独立。

segments.en: He loves to travel alone.
segments.zh: 他喜欢一个人旅行。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So it means that you don't really need other people's help, I guess, right?
segments.zh: 所以这意味着你真的不需要别人的帮助，我猜，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So he's not really very independent and well, his friend agrees.
segments.zh: 所以他不是真的很独立，嗯，他的朋友也同意这一点。

segments.en: He says, well, you know what?
segments.zh: 他说，嗯，你知道吗？

segments.en: I think she has a point.
segments.zh: 我认为她有道理。

segments.en: To have a point means to say something that the other person agrees with.
segments.zh: To have a point 的意思是说出的观点对方也认同。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So you could say, he has a point.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，他有道理。

segments.en: I agree with him.
segments.zh: 我同意他的看法。

segments.en: That's a good argument.
segments.zh: 这是一个很好的论点。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So if somebody says something and you agree with that, when you say, yeah, you have a point, it means you agree with the argument.
segments.zh: 因此，如果有人说了什么而你同意，当你说“是的，你有道理”时，就意味着你同意他的观点。

segments.en: You agree with what that person says.
segments.zh: 你同意那个人所说的话。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And now lastly, because he lives with his parents, his friend is saying that he should move out.
segments.zh: 最后，因为他和父母住在一起，他的朋友说他应该搬出去。

segments.en: You should move out.
segments.zh: 你应该搬出去。

segments.en: So here's another phrasal verb, to move out.
segments.zh: 所以这是另一个短语动词，to move out（搬出去）。

segments.en: This means that you leave the house and you find a new house.
segments.zh: 这意味着你离开家，你找到了一所新房子。

segments.en: So when you're with your parents, you want to move out.
segments.zh: 所以当你和你的父母在一起时，你想搬出去。

segments.en: That means you don't live with your parents anymore, but you find your own house.
segments.zh: 这意味着你不再和你的父母住在一起，但你找到了自己的房子。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, well, in general, when you find your own house, when you leave and your current place of living, that's moving out, right?
segments.zh: 所以，好吧，总的来说，当你找到自己的房子，当你离开和你现在的居住地时，那就搬出去了，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So if I'm leaving the city, I move out of my house.
segments.zh: 所以如果我离开城市，我会搬出我的房子。

segments.en: And then when I arrive in a new city, I move in to a new house.
segments.zh: 然后当我到达一个新城市时，我搬进了一个新房子。

segments.en: Oh, very good.
segments.zh: 哦，非常好。

segments.en: So to move out and to move in, they go hand in hand.
segments.zh: 所以搬出去和搬进来是相辅相成的。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: The phrase is manning up.
segments.zh: 这个短语是 man up（拿出担当）。

segments.en: So the girlfriend was tired of the man not manning up.
segments.zh: 所以女朋友受够了那个男人不肯拿出担当。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So to man up.
segments.zh: 所以要 man up（拿出担当）。

segments.en: And what does that mean?
segments.zh: 那是什么意思？

segments.en: To man up to something?
segments.zh: man up 是说要担起某事？

segments.en: It means to be responsible or to be more mature or to be an adult about something.
segments.zh: 这意味着对某事负责或更成熟或成为成年人。

segments.en: So maybe this guy, this man, he's kind of immature.
segments.zh: 所以也许这个人，这个人，他有点不成熟。

segments.en: He lives at home.
segments.zh: 他住在家里。

segments.en: He's not very responsible or independent.
segments.zh: 他不是很负责任或独立。

segments.en: And his girlfriend wanted him to be more responsible, more independent.
segments.zh: 而他的女朋友希望他更有责任感，更独立。

segments.en: So she wanted him to man up.
segments.zh: 所以她想让他拿出担当。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it usually means that you also should accept the consequences for your actions.
segments.zh: 所以这通常意味着你也应该接受你的行为的后果。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So you might push someone to man up, take responsibility for something and do it even though the consequences might not be fun or good.
segments.zh: 所以你可能会促使某人拿出担当，为某事负责并去做，即使后果可能不好受。

segments.en: Now this remember is very, very much slang.
segments.zh: 记住，这个说法非常非常俚语化。

segments.en: So you don't say this in an essay or a paper.
segments.zh: 所以你不会在论文或论文中这么说。

segments.en: This is what you say between friends.
segments.zh: 这就是你在朋友之间说的话。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And another slang phrase here that we use to describe this man is a mama's boy.
segments.zh: 这里的另一个俚语是 a mama's boy，我们用它来形容这个男人。

segments.en: He says, his friend says he's a mama's boy.

segments.en: Mama's boy.

segments.en: So mama is mother.

segments.en: Mama's boy means that he's very, very close with his mother.
segments.zh: 妈宝男的意思是他和妈妈非常非常亲近。

segments.en: This is not a good thing to say.
segments.zh: 这不是一件好事。

segments.en: It's usually something that's a little bit critical.
segments.zh: 这通常是有点关键的事情。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So say he's a mama's boy.

segments.en: Okay.

segments.en: Right.

segments.en: And he doesn't do anything for himself.

segments.en: He's like a little baby.

segments.en: He's like a child and his mama, his mother does everything for him.

segments.en: So it is a little bit like an insult, I guess.
segments.zh: 所以这有点像侮辱，我猜。

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So it's not really a good thing to call someone a mama's boy unless in this situation, they're friends and his friend is saying, well, you know what?

segments.en: It seems like you're a mama's boy.

segments.en: Exactly.

segments.en: All right.

segments.en: So our next phrase is when he was justifying and say, why would I move out?

segments.en: Why would I leave my parents' house?

segments.en: I have a great roof over my head.

segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So the roof means the top of your house.
segments.zh: 所以屋顶意味着你家的顶部。

segments.en: You know, obviously our houses, they're not open.
segments.zh: 你知道，显然我们的房子，它们不是敞开的。

segments.en: They have a cover and that's called a roof.
segments.zh: 它们有一个顶盖，这就叫屋顶。

segments.en: But the phrase here, a roof over my head or a roof over one's head means a place to live.
segments.zh: 但这里的短语，我头上的屋顶或头顶的屋顶意味着住的地方。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: A home.

segments.en: So if you say, I don't have a roof over my head, that means I don't have a home.

segments.en: I don't have a house.

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So he's saying that he has a great roof over his head.

segments.en: His mom does everything for him.

segments.en: So he's like, why would I move out?
segments.zh: 所以他想，我为什么要搬出去？

segments.en: And his friend ends the conversation by saying, you know what?

segments.en: Let's agree to disagree.
segments.zh: 看来我们只能各持己见了。

segments.en: This is a really important phrase to learn, especially if you like to argue a lot.
segments.zh: 这是一个非常重要的短语，特别是如果你喜欢争论的话。

segments.en: In this case, one guy said, listen, living at home is good.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，一个人说，听着，住在家里是好的。

segments.en: It works for me.
segments.zh: 它对我有用。

segments.en: And the other said, no, it's not very responsible.
segments.zh: 另一个说，不，这不是很负责。

segments.en: I agree with your girlfriend.
segments.zh: 我同意你的女朋友。

segments.en: And at the end, they still believe what they thought originally.
segments.zh: 最后，他们仍然相信他们最初的想法。

segments.en: So they agree to disagree.
segments.zh: 所以他们同意各持己见。

segments.en: That means they're not going to argue anymore, but they're not going to change their minds.
segments.zh: 这意味着他们不会再争论，但他们不会改变主意。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So I respect your opinion and you respect my opinion and the conversation is over.
segments.zh: 所以我尊重你的意见，你尊重我的意见，谈话结束了。

segments.zh: 一个男人还能求什么？

segments.en: Let's agree to disagree.
segments.zh: 看来我们只能各持己见了。

segments.en: All right, so talking about a mama's boy living at home.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以说到妈宝男住在家里。

segments.en: Now, as he mentioned, in the United States, kids usually leave home when they're 18 or 19 when they go to college, right?
segments.zh: 现在，正如他所提到的，在美国，孩子上大学时通常在 18 岁或 19 岁时离开家，对吧？

segments.en: But in other places, like in Latin America or even, for example, in many parts of Europe, people will live at home until they're 24 or 26 because it is expensive to live by yourself.
segments.zh: 但在其他地方，比如在拉丁美洲，甚至在欧洲的许多地方，人们会一直住在家里，直到他们 24 或 26 岁，因为一个人住很贵。

segments.en: It is, and so in a lot of these countries, you hear people maybe joking about the men being mama's boys.
segments.zh: 确实如此，在很多国家，你可能会听到人们开玩笑说男人是妈宝男。

segments.en: Like Italy, for example, this is often something that people like to joke about.
segments.zh: 例如，像意大利一样，这通常是人们喜欢开玩笑的事情。

segments.en: Obviously, it's not true in most cases, but it is true that a lot of people live with their families until later because, like you say, it's expensive or maybe in their culture, in their tradition, you don't leave your home until you get married.
segments.zh: 显然，在大多数情况下并非如此，但确实有很多人与家人住在一起，直到后来，因为就像你说的那样，这很昂贵，或者在他们的文化中，在他们的传统中，你在结婚之前不会离开家。

segments.en: Right, because it could be also for religious reasons.
segments.zh: 对，因为它也可能是出于宗教原因。

segments.en: Exactly, and so I think it differs from culture to culture, but this idea of a mama's boy is very, very much a part of American culture.
segments.zh: 没错，所以我认为它因文化而异，但妈宝男这种观念是美国文化中很典型的一部分。

segments.en: We often talk about this.
segments.zh: 我们经常谈论这个。

segments.en: We often joke about it, and sometimes you say, oh, you're such a mama's boy because my brother sometimes, he calls my mom a lot.
segments.zh: 我们经常拿它开玩笑，有时你会说，哦，你真是个妈宝男，因为有时我兄弟老是给我妈妈打电话。

segments.en: I say, oh, you're such a mama's boy, always calling mom.
segments.zh: 我说，哦，你真是个妈宝男，老是给妈妈打电话。

segments.en: Now, obviously, this works for guys, but what about girls?
segments.zh: 现在，显然，这适用于男人，但是女孩呢？

segments.en: Would you say like daddy's girl?
segments.zh: 你会说 daddy's girl 吗？

segments.en: Yeah, a little bit.
segments.zh: 是的，一点点。

segments.en: It's usually girls who get everything they want from their dads.
segments.zh: 通常是女孩从父亲那里得到她们想要的一切。

segments.en: Like, daddy, I want a new car.
segments.zh: 就像，爸爸，我想要一辆新车。

segments.en: Daddy, I want new clothes.
segments.zh: 爸爸，我想要新衣服。

segments.en: Yeah, so daddy's girl is someone who is very close with their dad and maybe is able to have him give her lots of stuff that she wants.
segments.zh: 是的，所以 daddy's girl 是指和爸爸非常亲近的人，也许能让爸爸给她很多她想要的东西。

segments.en: So we don't really hear like daddy's boy or mama's girl very often, right?
segments.zh: 所以我们不太常听到 daddy's boy 或 mama's girl 这种说法，对吧？

segments.en: No, it's the opposite.
segments.zh: 不，情况正好相反。

segments.en: It's always the opposite.
segments.zh: 总是相反的。

segments.en: Yeah, yeah, exactly.
segments.zh: 是的，是的，没错。

segments.en: Well, it's a very interesting topic, and I'm sure many of you in your different cultures may also continue living with your parents, or maybe it's not common, or maybe even after marriage in many parts of Asia, people get married and live at home with their in-laws.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是一个非常有趣的话题，我相信你们中的许多人可能也会继续与父母住在一起，或者这可能并不常见，甚至在亚洲许多地区结婚后，人们结婚并与姻亲一起生活在家里。

segments.en: That's right, so we're very curious to hear about your experience in your country.
segments.zh: 没错，所以我们很想知道您在贵国的经历。

segments.en: If you have such a thing as a mama's boy or a daddy's girl, let us know.
segments.zh: 如果你们那里也有妈宝男或 daddy's girl 这种说法，请告诉我们。

segments.en: Our website is EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 我们的网站是 EnglishPod.com。

segments.en: All right, we'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 好，到时候在那里见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
